card.thesis: Even with a big down payment, veterans' home loans have still priced below the best conventional tier, so their upfront fee has paid back within a few years.
card.overturns: "With a big down payment, a conventional loan beats paying the veteran loan fee."

claim: Common advice says a veteran who can put 20% down should skip the VA loan, because conventional loans then need no mortgage insurance and the VA charges an upfront fee (1.25% of the loan with 10% or more down). But in daily locked-rate data, the average VA rate was below the average rate for the best conventional tier (credit score 740+, 20% or more down) on 92.4% of days since January 2017 and on 99.9% of days since the current fee table took effect in April 2023, by 0.32 points on average (6.261% vs 6.581%). At those averages a $100,000 VA loan pays about $20.97 less per month; counting both the lower payment and the faster-shrinking balance, the $1,250 fee is recovered after 47 months, and after 10 years the VA borrower is about $1,952 ahead per $100,000. Veterans receiving disability compensation pay no fee at all. This is history, not a forecast.

assumptions: The VA index averages all VA locks (every credit score and down payment) while the conventional comparator is its best tier (740+, 20%+ down); if VA pricing improves with credit score as conventional pricing does, this understates the gap for a strong-credit veteran. Individual quotes differ.
First-use or subsequent-use purchase loan with at least 10% down, fee 1.25% (fee table row (D)(iii)), paid in cash; financing the fee would add interest.
No mortgage insurance on either loan, same loan amount, same 30-year term, no refinancing; closing costs other than the VA fee assumed equal; undiscounted dollars.
limits: History, not a forecast. Index averages are not quotes; VA loans can differ in appraisal and closing requirements and in the mix of borrowers behind the average. A borrower who sells or refinances before the payback point loses on the fee. The 1.25% fee applies to loans closed from April 7, 2023 until June 9, 2034 under the current table.
